item.title: Sisters who visited Llandudno drowned at beauty spot in Eryri, inquest hears
item.description: Married mother-of-two Hajra Zahid, 29, and her sister Haleema, 25, were pulled from pools on the Watkin Path which leads to the Yr Wyddfa summit.

item.title: Why traffic is being held and speed restrictions are in place on the A55 today
item.description: This is due to impact traffic at Junction 18, Llandudno Junction.

item.title: Excitement as Colwyn Bay Market returns – Saturday plans and events in the works
item.description: The market’s comeback, under the management of Together For Colwyn Bay, signalled a welcome return for the town, its traders, and shoppers.

item.title: North Wales man David Taylor and two others bailed over alleged spying for China
item.description: The husband of a Labour MP and two other men have been released on bail after being arrested on suspicion of spying for China.

item.title: Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board to remain in special measures
item.description: The report comes amid serious and horrifying incidents, including an elderly woman who died alone in a corridor in full view of other patients.

item.title: Welsh Mountain Zoo keepers support Chimpanzee cradling stillborn baby
item.description: The mother, Mellony, is currently holding her infant — behaviour that experts say is natural and instinctive among chimpanzees following such a loss.

item.title: Imagination takes centre stage as children dress up for World Book Day
item.description: World Book Day always brings a burst of colour, imagination and pure joy to classrooms and communities across North Wales, and this year’s celebrations were no exception.

item.title: Gwrych Castle stars in Sky History series highlighting lottery-funded restorations
item.description: Great British Castle Rescue, a new three-part series presented by Rick Edwards, will focus on some of the UK’s most endangered castles.

item.title: Former North Wales railway station turned country home on the market for £825K
item.description: Passenger services on the route ended in 1953, with the last goods train running in 1962, after which Eyarth Station closed.

item.title: 'Serious concern' for man missing from Derbyshire who could be in Llandudno
item.description: Serious concerns for the safety of Tony, known to visit Llandudno and the wider area, have been raised by police.
